title: Hierarchical Planning, stage H0: does the engine obey the plan? The check, the gate and the baseline
request: The owner asked for the Hierarchical Planning work to be reviewed, implemented correctly, improved and tested on several models, and agreed that more structure is a risk: at least review and improve the planning. The approved plan starts by measuring, with a gate fixed before any change.
spec: A check by code, with no model, that says for a built project whether each trap its plan caught was enforced; a gate for the whole repair, pinned before the first fix; a baseline read from a live run kept before the repair.
plan: three audits: the document pack as a checklist, the planning code against it, the execution code against it
a pure function that reads the caught traps against the solution, the final features and the split
the gate of the repair, every check named, pinned by its hash
the baseline stored as the campaign's first result

decisions.decision: A trap code cannot enforce is never counted as enforced
decisions.why: a cost asymmetry or a missing horizon is a thing to say to the person, and counting it would make any report look obeyed

decisions.decision: A column absent from the final model by luck is not enforced
decisions.why: nothing forbids it, so the next run may use it

decisions.decision: A build that paused with a question and then went on is not a build that stopped
decisions.why: in the kept run a project asked, built anyway and used a random split where its plan asked for a split by time

decisions.decision: The baseline is read from a kept run, at no cost
decisions.why: the run was made before this work, so nobody could tune it

decisions.decision: The larger team design of the document pack is not built
decisions.why: measurements of the same week show that added roles and calls lowered the score and the time

change: A module that reads whether a built project obeyed its plan, a campaign with its gate and its first result, and the mapping of the campaign into the bench layers.

findings.defect: No trap a plan caught was enforced in the built project, in a run where every scenario was reported as passed.
findings.scenario: A plan caught a column recorded after the outcome; the project's forbidden list was empty and the column was the top feature of the final model. Three plans asked for a split by time and the data stage used a stratified random split.
findings.cause: the plan is saved and shown, and the engine never reads it
findings.fix: Stage H2 of the plan: a caught trap becomes a change to the project's solution through the validated move, or stops the build with a question.
findings.open: the fix is stage H2; this package only measures

findings.defect: The first form of the check counted a project that paused with a question as having obeyed its plan.
findings.scenario: A scenario asked the person a question, went on, built and used a random split; its two traps were left out of the count.
findings.cause: a pause was read as a stop
findings.fix: A stop is a pause with no final stage.

measurements.name: The baseline: traps caught against traps enforced, on a kept live run
measurements.gate: hp_gate_v1, check one: every enforceable trap a plan caught is enforced, or the build stopped with a question
measurements.result: five projects, all reported as passed; thirty-three traps caught, eight that code can enforce, none enforced
measurements.next: stage H1 (the defects that block a project) and stage H2 (the plan drives the engine)
limits: five invented tables from one run and one model
a trap is read from its name and the column it ends with
the gate's other checks are not read here

outcome: The check, the pinned gate and the baseline exist; the baseline fails the gate's first check, as the audit predicted. No behaviour of the product changed.
lessons: A scenario that passes because it finished says nothing about whether the plan was followed.
Measure what the built thing did, not what the plan said.
risks: Reading a trap from its name will miss traps named differently.
A check that only counts can be passed by catching fewer traps: the gate's second check, nothing lost, guards that.
